the S-enantiomer of zopiclone (ChEMBL parent CHEMBL1522), a drug of its own with its own label; split because whether the enantiomers act differently is not known: GtoPdb holds no interaction for either and the US and UK labels describe one site without comparing them (Fable pass of 8 November 2026, decision 9.121 C5)

the d-enantiomer of amphetamine (ChEMBL parent CHEMBL612), a drug of its own with its own label; split because the enantiomers act differently: the l-isomer was twice as potent as the d-isomer on basal fronto-cortical noradrenaline release while the d-isomer dominates striatal dopamine release (Easton et al. 2006, doi:10.1016/j.neuropharm.2006.07.035) (Fable pass of 8 November 2026, decision 9.121 C5)
